stories.title: Australia's first-ever Michelin stars go to 11 restaurants in one state
stories.summary: Australia has been awarded its first Michelin stars, with 11 restaurants in the state of South Australia receiving the distinction. Magill Estate Restaurant in Adelaide was the only venue to receive two stars, while 10 others were awarded one star each. South Australia's government paid for incognito inspectors to visit the state, according to national broadcaster ABC, which is why no spots have been recognised in other parts of the country. Magill chef and owner Scott Huggins said he had "dreamt of working in Michelin star restaurants as a youngster". He said he had worked in Michelin star restaurants in Europe and Japan.

stories.title: New chip-scale gyroscope measures rotation with unprecedented sensitivity
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a chip-scale optical ring-laser gyroscope that can measure rotation as slow as 37 degrees per hour. This record sensitivity, approaching Earth's rotation rate of 15 degrees per hour, could eventually be useful for precision navigation and orientation systems, particularly where GPS is unavailable. Gyroscopes measure how an object rotates, helping determine its orientation and movement. The chip-based gyroscopes found in smartphones and other everyday devices tend to have limited sensitivity, making them unsuitable for some demanding applications. This has driven scientists to develop chip-based versions of optical gyroscopes, which are sensitive enough for applications such as aircraft navigation.

stories.title: Scientists identify avian cholera as major cause of penguin deaths in Antarctica
stories.summary: Thousands of Adélie penguins found dead in Antarctica in 2024 were primarily victims of avian cholera, not high pathogenicity avian influenza (H5N1) as researchers initially suspected, according to a study published today in Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences. The findings highlight an underrecognized threat to Antarctic wildlife and the importance of comprehensive disease investigations, particularly as H5N1 continues to raise concerns for seabird and marine mammal populations. In March 2024, an international research expedition visited Antarctica's remote Danger Islands, home to more than 1.2 million breeding pairs of Adélie penguins. Researchers discovered thousands of dead penguins across two islands, along with carcasses of several other seabird species.

stories.title: Dogs Seem to Agree With Humans That 'Bouba' Is Round And 'Kiki' Is Spiky
stories.summary: Picture a shape called 'Bouba'. What features does it have? Is it angular, rounded, soft, hard? What about a shape called 'Kiki'? There's no correct answer to this – the words are made up. But for some strange reason, most people who are asked this question – regardless of the language or alphabet they use to speak or write – agree that Kiki is spiky, and Bouba is round. This fascinating psychological experiment was first conceived in the 1920s, and it suggests there may be something universal about the way we humans connect visual information, like shapes, with sounds.

stories.title: Student protesters attack government buildings in Albania
stories.summary: Thousands of students have taken to the streets in the Albanian capital of Tirana, attacking several government buildings on the second day of violent anti-government protests. The demonstration began outside the ministry of education on Tuesday, as students called for better university conditions and job prospects. Wednesday saw part of the education ministry's building set on fire, while the prime minister's office, finance and interior ministry, and several surrounding businesses were also attacked. Albania's Deputy Prime Minister ​Albana Koçiu has called for "calmness, self-restraint and maturity" and said "Albania does not need to burn to change".
